paper_metadata.title: Cross-kink unpinning controls the medium- to high-temperature strength of body-centered cubic NbTiZr medium-entropy alloy

Most notably, the present experimental observations suggest that cross-kink unpinning is the controlling strengthening mechanism at intermediate to high temperatures
the Peierls contribution to the overall strength is negligible above 400 K, but both the Peierls and cross-kink mechanisms contribute to the strength below 400 K.
TEM investigations show that the alloy deformation is controlled by screw-dislocation slip.
The TEM investigations at 1073 K are consistent with the annihilation of cross-kinks/edge dipoles, which can explain the observed strength drop above this temperature.

At yet higher temperatures (1073 K), the microstructure showed dislocations arranged into a honeycomb-like structure, presumably formed due to the activation of recovery processes like dislocation climb.

Therefore, the present experimental observations suggest that interstitial solutes like C and/or O strongly interact with dislocations and facilitate the occurrence of the PLC effect in NbTiZr BCC-MEA at 473 K.

The observed straight dislocations and debris at low temperatures (77 K) are consistent with the screw dislocation theory prediction of cross-kink and Peierls strengthening as the controlling mechanisms of screw dislocation strength at low temperatures.

At moderate temperatures (300 K, 473 K), the presence of less straight segments and the dominance of debris and dislocation loops behind the dislocations confirm that cross-kink strengthening is the controlling strengthening mechanism as temperature increases.

Above 300 K, since the strength of NbTiZr is controlled by cross-kinks, the break-away energy barrier of screw dislocations off the cross-kinks can be very large. Due to this, the strength of the alloy becomes almost insensitive to the deformation temperature leading to a plateau region
The TEM investigations at 1073 K are consistent with the annihilation of cross-kinks/edge dipoles, which can explain the observed strength drop above this temperature.
The experimentally measured V ∗ ∼ 8 b 3 at 77 K is consistent with the Peierls mechanisms controlling the low temperature strength.

The occurrence of serrations and negative strain-rate sensitivity has been considered to be the classical signature of dynamic strain-aging (DSA), often referred to as Portevin-Lechatelier (PLC) effect
Interestingly, in addition to notable strain-hardening, the stress-strain curve at 473 K showed serrations (see inset in Fig. 1 (b)).

According to Maresca and Curtin, at high temperatures, the vacancy cross-kinks can be mobile enough to glide along the screw dislocation, eventually leading to annihilation (vacancy cross-kinks annihilating with self-interstitial cross-kinks) and the loss of strength.
Microstructural investigations revealed that plastic deformation occurred only by dislocation glide with no twinning involved, and was controlled by screw dislocations.

conflicts.subject: NbTiZr yield strength at room temperature (tension vs compression vs literature)
conflicts.description: The present tensile YS at 300 K (630 MPa) is lower than the as-cast compression YS measured at room temperature (695 MPa) and both are significantly lower than the compression data reported by Senkov et al.; the authors attribute differences to tension/compression response, specimen characteristics and small compositional differences.
